public_body: Cape & Vineyard Electric Co-Op Executive Committee
overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the February 10, 2011 minutes were accurate because the wind turbine topic was not discussed, and no evidence showed an illegal meeting to approve the letter. It noted, without a finding, that approving the minutes took 17 months.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Feb 10, 2011 Executive Committee minutes were inaccurate because they omitted a summary of discussion on proposed Cape Cod Commission wind turbine regulations.
allegations.key_passage: Because there is no evidence that the Executive Committee discussed the wind turbine topic during the meeting, we find the February 10, 2011 minutes are accurate.

allegations.summary: In the alternative, complaint alleged the committee must have discussed and approved the letter to the Cape Cod Commission outside an open meeting before it was submitted.
allegations.key_passage: We find no evidence that the Executive Committee discussed this matter outside of a meeting, and credit the Executive Committee's assertion that President McLaughlin signed and submitted the letter on his own without the Executive Committee's formal approval.

allegations.summary: Not alleged in the complaint: the AG observed that the committee took 17 months to approve the February 10, 2011 open session minutes.
allegations.key_passage: While the Executive Committee did create minutes of this meeting, it took 17 months to approve them, thus approval was not timely.
